answer: A harbor authority can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a refundable deposit before docking, turning cheap fake identities into a real cost. Reputation then flows like water through a lagoon: a newcomer starts at the shallow edge and only earns deep-water privileges after repeated, verified trades with distinct peers. Each trade is recorded as a vertex in a trust graph, so a cluster of identities that only vouch for each other forms a visible, isolated clique that the harbor can quarantine without punishing honest newcomers.
